title: New models: SiteDocument and SiteDocumentVersion (catalogue rows; the documents live in S3)
description:
Outcome: The site's configuration becomes data: the SiteConfig document, the BrandPack, the nav, and authored pages that are not Items. DynamoDB holds only the catalogue (standing rule: never text in DynamoDB). SiteDocument: id "<tenant>#<kind>" (kind: site | brand | nav), tenantId, kind, currentVersion, s3Key, sha256, schemaVersion, updatedBy, updatedAt. SiteDocumentVersion: id "<tenant>#<kind>#<version>", documentId, version, s3Key, sha256, createdBy, createdAt, note; index documentId sorted by version. Bodies at tenants/<tenant>/site/<kind>/<version>.json. A save writes a new version object, then moves currentVersion with a conditional update, so a half-written save is never live. Dedicated sites seed these from their repository files at deploy (the file-seeded store of PPY-f0ae90).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/data/schema.ts, amplify/data/resource.ts, src/papyrus_content (new site_store module, used by PPY-f0ae90), amplify/storage paths (tenants/<t>/site/).

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/site-documents.feature):
Scenario: A brand change is a new version
    Given "alpha" has brand version 3
    When an admin saves new colours
    Then version 4 is written to S3 and SiteDocument points at it only after the object exists

Scenario: An older version can be restored
    Given "alpha" has brand versions 1 to 4
    When an admin restores version 2
    Then version 5 is written with version 2's content

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-31c45c. Blocks PPY-70a429, PPY-e572de. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-f0ae90.

Testing: pytest for the store (moto for S3), Behave in a sandbox.
Rollout: Releasable alone. Index: new tables only.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the store and S3 disagree after a crash. Mitigation: the row moves only after the object exists; an orphan object is harmless and listed by a repair command.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: new tables only: SiteDocumentVersion (documentId + version).
AppSync authorisation: changes: new models (tenant admin write via claims).
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
